short: CTC decoder (M06), concatenated training sentences (M03) and six IMUs (M05) are standard: CTC silent-phrase decoding predates it; 97.17% is a word ratio on 4 people, split unstated.
position: The paper [@xie2025sixaxis] changes the decoder (M06, Conformer with CTC), the training data (M03, concatenated words plus noise) and the sensing (M05, six six-axis IMUs); all three are standard. Continuous silent recognition (8.9% WER, 2,200 words) [@meltzner2018semg] and CTC decoding of silent phrases [@chen2023hdsemg; @benster2024mona] predate it, and the cited Luo et al. already trained CTC for silent sentences [@luo2020acoustic], so the §1 novelty claim fails (Appendix). Liu et al. trained IMU decoders on concatenated sentences and tested on spoken ones [@liu2024lipimu]; this paper does not say whether its length curve (Fig. 3a) scores recorded or concatenated sequences. The headline 97.17% is a word ratio on 4 participants with a 70:15:15 split of unstated unit; repetition leakage across it is not excluded (M12).
